obligations.text: An ExternalName can be used in commands in place of the module name (lookup by stored Name first, then ExternalName).
obligations.cases: command naming a module by its ExternalName vs by Name vs neither
obligations.gap: Name-then-ExternalName precedence is modeled only for show (thin_surfaces inspection_choice) and uninstall (uninstall.rs lookup_m); other commands that accept a module name (load/update/install, module-action, list-dependents) have no model of alias resolution, so "commands" in general is not distinguished.

obligations.text: An ExternalName must be unique and must not match another module's name; saving a manifest that violates this is refused.
obligations.cases: new module with ExternalName equal to another module's Name or ExternalName vs a unique ExternalName
obligations.gap: No model of the ExternalName validation in Storage/Module.cls %OnValidateObject. Contrast: loading module B with ExternalName "a" while module a is installed is refused with the stored record unchanged, vs a unique ExternalName that saves.

units.B1: excluded: definition listing resource attributes; each attribute rule is owned elsewhere (Scope: module.resource.scope; Deploy: module.deployed; Directory: module.placement)

parent.entailment: The parent owns processor selection and the dropped-resource rule, graded directly. Children add separate outcomes; nothing is composed.

obligations.text: IPM picks a resource processor for each listed resource from its type (extension) or element.
obligations.cases: .cls/.inc/.mac/path resource vs element-declared (e.g. <WebApplication>, <FileCopy>) resource
obligations.observation: processor class attached to the resource
obligations.gap: No model selects the processor class (ResourceReference processor resolution / Module default processor per extension). Chunk-A models take the processor as given (defaults#4 compares a named class). Contrast: a .cls resource gets the Document default processor while <FileCopy> gets FileCopy.

obligations.text: Loading a manifest that no longer lists a resource or dependency updates the stored record but leaves the dropped resource's code and the dropped dependency module installed (C:D26).
obligations.cases: reload with a resource and a dependency removed
obligations.observation: stored record lists vs class presence and dependency module presence
obligations.basis: reused:.g5/ontology/concepts/data-policy.g5.md metadata (iteration52; as-built frame of the load writer)

obligations.text: When saving a module, IPM refuses a new resource reference whose nonempty unique name is already stored (even for the same module); reusing the stored reference passes this check. The check uses the stored identity and unique name.
obligations.cases: new reference with stored name (refused) vs reused stored reference (allowed) vs empty unique name (allowed)

obligations.text: The duplicate check runs before a deployed-project installer can be called.
obligations.cases: duplicate (refused save) vs reused reference on the deployed-project path

obligations.text: A refused save can leave changed object fields that were not written to the row; the database must be read separately.
obligations.cases: refused duplicate save: object marked_deployed true vs database flag false; reused: database true

obligations.text: Reusing the stored reference still runs the other module save checks.
obligations.cases: reused reference with another failing save guard vs all guards pass
obligations.gap: resource_save_allowed is the only save guard modeled; no model combines it with the other %OnValidateObject checks (ExternalName clash, other-module ownership), so a reused reference that fails another guard is not distinguished from one that saves.

parent.entailment: Children (operations/namespaces page) own mapping commands; the per-namespace separation is the parent's own claim, graded directly and not composed.

obligations.text: IPM 0.9+ is installed per namespace: each namespace can have its own IPM version, repositories, installed modules and history.
obligations.cases: two namespaces with different local installs / registries / module records
obligations.observation: per-namespace IPM code, registry data, module records and history
obligations.gap: ns_mapping.rs separates IPM code, registry data and the zpm record per namespace (L1), but installed (non-IPM) module records and history rows are not represented per namespace. Contrast: installing module m in NS1 leaves NS2's module list and history unchanged. Note: config settings are instance-wide (metadata), which the "own repositories" wording does not qualify.

obligations.text: Each namespace has its own log and IPM writes a record in the namespace where the action runs.
obligations.cases: action run in NS1 vs NS2
obligations.observation: which namespace's history table gets the row
obligations.gap: No writer model has a namespace dimension (the load/history crate is single-namespace; history.rs only reads (ns,id) keys). Contrast: install in NS1 adds a row to NS1 only. Coverage map lists history.namespace as not modeled.

obligations.text: Record IDs are unique only within a namespace: a detail lookup is scoped to the namespace.
obligations.cases: same ID present in NS a, absent in NS b
obligations.basis: new:iteration-70 (extension history.rs, not linked from this block)

obligations.text: config set HistoryRetain <days> makes IPM delete records that started more than that many days ago; 0 (default) turns purging off.
obligations.cases: retain>0 with old and new rows vs retain 0
obligations.gap: purge takes the set of matching rows as an input (quoted_date_matches) instead of deriving it from the start time and the cutoff, and the retain=0 branch is defined but never exercised. Contrast: retain=7 deletes a 10-day-old row and keeps a 1-day-old row; retain=0 deletes neither and leaves the marker (General/History.cls purge, Main.cls:840-842).

obligations.text: The purge runs on any IPM command, at most once per calendar day.
obligations.cases: first vs second command on the same day; non-Shell entry
obligations.gap: The ran_today input is defined but only ran_today=false is exercised; no model of the daily marker comparison or of the Shell-only trigger (purge runs only through %IPM.Main:Shell). Contrast: second command same day deletes nothing even with an expired row.

obligations.text: The purge applies to every namespace, not just the current one.
obligations.cases: expired rows in NS1 and NS2, command run in NS1
obligations.gap: purge is single-namespace. Contrast: an expired row in another IPM namespace is deleted by a command in the current namespace.

obligations.text: As built, the daily marker advances whether or not anything was deleted, so it proves an attempt, not a deletion.
obligations.cases: first purge of the day with no matching rows

obligations.text: As built (P:F-HIST-6, G:D3), the quoted cutoff matches no row, so an expired row is kept.
obligations.cases: expired 2000-01-01 row with quoted vs unquoted cutoff
obligations.gap: The empty match set is an input to purge; no model derives it from the quoted SQL cutoff. The native control (unquoted cutoff deletes both old rows) is not represented as a neighbour.

obligations.text: The log survives uninstalling IPM itself: full cleanup removes all modules and IPM's metadata except the history log.
obligations.cases: uninstall of IPM with -all: module records/metadata globals vs ^IPM.General.HistoryD
obligations.observation: presence of history rows and of IPM metadata after cleanup
obligations.gap: uninstall.rs keeps hist only as a frame of clean_code and appends the IPM success row before Clean (OBS-H15); it has no IPM metadata globals, so "metadata removed, HistoryD kept" (Lifecycle/Module.cls Clean, :54) is not contrasted. Coverage map: not modeled.

obligations.text: Working assumption: uninstalling IPM in one namespace does not delete the history records (including in-progress ones) of other namespaces.
obligations.cases: IPM uninstall in NS1 with in-progress rows in NS2
obligations.gap: No multi-namespace model of IPM self-uninstall. Open question history.keep-on-ipm-uninstall.other-namespaces.
